title: One commit and one push per step, instead of per record
gloss: one commit and push per step
description:
A single reconcile end-to-end test performs 87 pushes: every durable record is its own commit AND its own push. In tests that is process cost; in production each push is a network round-trip to origin - and the network is where this run lost two and a half hours to a git fetch holding an ssh connection open with no bound.

Batching a step's records into one commit and one push would cut process count, wall clock and network exposure together. It is the largest single win in this epic.

It is also the one that changes MEANING, which is why it is its own tick and blocked on the plumbing work. Today each record lands separately and the compare-and-swap guarantees are stated per record; a batched commit changes what is atomic and what a resumed run sees when it reads a partially-written step. Do not start by writing code: start by stating which invariants the current per-record commits provide (Appendix A, the CAS rules in .ticfac/), which of them a per-step commit preserves, and which need a different mechanism. If any invariant cannot survive it, say so and stop - a faster run that loses a durability guarantee is not the trade this epic wants.
notes: 2026-10-05 15:37 - Invariant analysis (f61). Per-record commits gave: (1) create_if_absent answered against origin before the caller acts; (2) sha-guarded checkpoint update refuses a stale writer; (3) each record durable before the next, so a crash leaves a prefix; (4) the checkpoint HISTORY is one commit per state and CheckpointHistory readers (settledButNeverCollected, recordedRejection) read intermediate states; (5) a claim is on origin before its work starts; (6) a lost push ack is recognised as the writer's own (o82); (7) the run tag sits on the terminal checkpoint's commit. A held step (runstate/held.go, reconcile/step.go) keeps every record its own commit, chained, and sends the chain as ONE push. (4),(6) unchanged. (3): crash states shrink from every prefix to {none, all}, both already reachable, provided no effect outside the run is taken on a held record; steps are chosen only where that holds (no job start, branch push, gate, teardown or long wait). (1): creates are never held; they land at once carrying what was held before them, and a create that loses its guard answers its conflict as alone while the earlier records land. (5): Claim is never held. (7): terminal checkpoints never held. (2) EXPLICIT DECISION: inside a step a non-terminal checkpoint update answers updated provisionally; its guard is re-examined at release and at any Fetch in the step (which rebases the chain onto origin's new head). A lost guard lands NOTHING of the step (HeldConflict) and the run stops as a refused checkpoint stops it today. Nothing is ever written over a lost guard. Steps: dispatching cp + marker; a tick's close (publishing cp, note, close, closed cp); a role tick's close; a NOT READY review's adoptions/notes/re-review/placements (not the deciding); a duplicate's note+close. Measured on the fixture epic (TestAFixtureEpicLandsEachStepInOnePush): 72 -> 52 pushes in all, 66 -> 46 to the integration branch (1.43x; per tick 13 -> 9). Kill mid-step + resume: TestARunKilledMidStepResumesFromTheStateBeforeTheStep. What remains per tick is separated by effects (job start, collect's preserve pushes, merge push, gate). Next cut: ride the integrating checkpoint on the merge push (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A step's records reach origin as one commit and one push where the invariants allow it, with the analysis of which invariants were checked recorded on the tick. A resumed run reads a batched step correctly, including a run killed mid-step, and a test covers that. Push count for the same fixture epic drops materially (report before and after). No compare-and-swap guarantee is weakened without an explicit decision recorded here.
